doc.title: Konitz Lee — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: From Atlantic to Verve and Norman Granz
summary: He doesn't recall why he changed labels, and they discuss Granz and the Ralph Burns 'Free Forms' album.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: You recorded for Atlantic [Records] for three years basically. Fifty-five, fifty-six, fifty-seven, and then you went with Verve [Records]?
What went down there? You’re relationship with Atlantic just went the way of other things and Verve made you an offer?
Wrong guy to ask. I don’t remember. I just assumed that they didn’t renew the contract.
I’ve found it curious that you recorded with Verve because you don’t seem like a “Norman Granz” kind of guy.
I was one of the people that he didn’t come to the sessions which means . . . that he wasn’t a fan of mine or whatever. But he did come to one session that Ralph Burns did.
That’s in fifty-one, right? That Free Forms album that Ralph Burns did that you played on?
It’s kind of a “mood” music record.

That got re-issued in the late nineties. When Verve put out that record you did with Jimmy Giuffre and the sax section and to fill out a two-record set they put that Ralph Burns thing on and they put a couple of Giuffre’s orchestral things that he did in Germany on it as well.
